nodes.text: What follows outdoes the dreadful look of this dream. When the forces of Mark Antony had been broken at Actium, Cassius of Parma, who had followed his side, fled to Athens. There, as he lay in bed at dead of night, his mind lulled to sleep after anxieties and cares, he thought that a man of huge size came to him, black in colour, filthy, with beard and hair grown long, and that when asked who he was he answered: *kakon daimona* ['an evil spirit']. Then, terrified by the hideous sight and the horrible name, he called out to his slaves and asked whether they had seen anyone of such appearance either entering or leaving the bedroom. When they declared that no one had come in there, he gave himself again to rest and sleep, and the same apparition hovered before his mind. So, sleep put to flight, he ordered a light to be brought in and forbade his slaves to leave him. Between this night and the capital punishment that Caesar inflicted on him only a very little time passed.
